svg.font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Who writes the bundle, and what checks it
svg.desc: Every write to the bundle goes one of four ways. The librarian, an agent, writes one file only, .lokf/patch.yaml, which the pen, knowledge-apply.sh, applies to the bundle; the pen refuses a human: actor. The curator, a named person, writes a verdict to the concept directly. The copy editor, ktl-prose, rewords what an agent wrote. The KTL Registrar plugin writes a lokf:related block and diataxis.md. The bundle is .lokf/knowledge/: one Markdown file per concept, with index.md and log.md in every folder. A reader's entry is kept beside the bundle. The docent answers readers and does not write in the bundle; knowledge-feedback.sh records a reader's entry in .lokf/feedback.md, what readers missed or disputed, which is input for the librarian. The pen moves each entry that the librarian handles into .lokf/questions.md. Programs check every write, and compute every label. The gate, knowledge-registrar.yaml, runs on each pull request that touches the bundle: lokf validate, the conventions script and the provenance check. A human: event needs that person's approval of the pull request, or their signature on the commit. The report, knowledge-report.sh, computes on every read each trust label, the health line, and what the curator and the librarian check next. A label is computed each time, and never stored.
